LESSON: OBLIQUE PROJECTION

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.1: Oblique Projection

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Oblique Projection. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How are oblique drawings used in technical fields?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the characteristics of oblique drawing in technical fields
2. draw shaped blocks in oblique projection
3. appreciate the application of oblique projection in drawing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: OBLIQUE PROJECTION
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Oblique Projection helps you succeed in PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

KEY FACTS: OBLIQUE PROJECTION
Study Oblique Projection like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain the characteristics of oblique drawing in technical fields

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the characteristics of oblique drawing in technical fields. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the characteristics of oblique drawing in technical fields.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Safety first: State one safety rule before practising “Oblique Projection”.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the characteristics of oblique drawing in technical fields. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Draw shaped blocks in oblique projection

What this means
In this part you learn to draw shaped blocks in oblique projection. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: draw shaped blocks in oblique projection.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Steps: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Oblique Projection.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can draw shaped blocks in oblique projection. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the application of oblique projection in drawing

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the application of oblique projection in drawing. You will use ideas from in the workshop corner, classroom, or a safe practice space.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the application of oblique projection in drawing.
2. Plan safely, do the steps, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Check: Inspect your work and say one improvement.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the application of oblique projection in drawing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Oblique Projection is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: State one safety rule before practising “Oblique Projection”. (skill: explain the characteristics of oblique drawing in technical fields)

Example 2: List 3 correct steps to complete a simple task on Oblique Projection. (skill: draw shaped blocks in oblique projection)

Example 3: Inspect your work and say one improvement. (skill: appreciate the application of oblique projection in drawing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Oblique Projection to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain the characteristics of oblique drawing in technical fields.
3. Practise this skill: draw shaped blocks in oblique projection.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the application of oblique projection in drawing.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Oblique Projection from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Oblique Projection: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Oblique Projection?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How are oblique drawings used in technical fields?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Oblique Projection means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain the characteristics of oblique drawing in technical fields.
5. Be able to: draw shaped blocks in oblique projection.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
